facts.resource_count_limit: Exact source-listed labels, deduplicated within each match. They include uncertain or offensive entries and are not verified forced-resource frequencies.
facts.cc_count_limit: Literal mentions in observed notes, including negated/uncertain/post-death mentions. These are search aids, not counts of landed CC.
facts.recovery_count_limit: Field coverage only: texts may explicitly say no reset. Not a reset-event rate.

hypotheses.statement: One opening target also explains every reported enemy kill in wins.
hypotheses.limitation: Descriptive endpoint comparison. Does not establish intended kill target, causes, or conditional win probability.

hypotheses.statement: A reachable enemy is losing meaningful health while partner disruption limits recovery or counterpressure long enough to finish. This is a useful conversion state, not a proven necessary or sufficient condition.
hypotheses.limitation: Mandatory double-Trinket removal, mandatory Warrior Blind, continuous partner isolation, and an inevitable Paladin kill all fail as universal rules. Some kills succeed with escapes ready or the partner active; a Paladin kill can still lose the round.

hypotheses.statement: A stronger fixed resource/target/control prerequisite is necessary.
hypotheses.limitation: Mandatory double-Trinket removal, mandatory Warrior Blind, continuous partner isolation, and an inevitable Paladin kill all fail as universal rules. Some kills succeed with escapes ready or the partner active; a Paladin kill can still lose the round.

opening_target.text: Arms Warrior; recorded in 69/80 games. This is the labeled opening target, not necessarily the first sustained coordinated damage.

initial_objective.text: Use Warrior pressure to develop a damaging window; decide between a covered Paladin commitment and continued Warrior pressure from the actual health and control state.

win_condition.text: A reachable enemy is losing meaningful health while partner disruption limits recovery or counterpressure long enough to finish. This is a useful conversion state, not a proven necessary or sufficient condition.

manufacture.text: Open Warrior in the usual line, pair pressure with Paladin control, and watch the response. Repeated healed Warrior attempts can lead to Warrior control and a Paladin swap; a low Warrior can instead be finished.

conversion.text: Commit to the vulnerable target and renew short control or interrupts around the health decline. Warrior Blind/Sap into Paladin damage is a repeated line; it is not the only winning line.

reset.text: After a Paladin immunity or healed attempt, return pressure to Warrior and stabilise; renew Paladin pressure when immunity ends if a fresh window exists. Recheck cooldowns after long exchanges.

assessment.text: Conditional control-window resource. Escapes and recovered cooldowns change the available control, but neither enemy Trinket is a universal pre-kill requirement.

failure_modes.text: A Paladin low is protected by Divine Shield; later resource expenditure fails to recreate the low-health window before a friendly death.
The first enemy kill is followed by a lost survival/cleanup exchange.

automatic_candidates.signal: Verified cast/aura, present health, or an observed control start/end
automatic_candidates.scope: Raw events only; not strategic intent or reliable absence of an enemy cooldown.
automatic_candidates.limitation: No addon implementation or API testing was performed; no automatic transition is certified.

manual_possible.confirmation: A meaningful enemy health window, current partner control and friendly readiness overlap.
Target recovered or became protected; team needs a new usable attempt.

web_only: Full comparison with losses and unresolved evidence

uncertainties: Mandatory double-Trinket removal, mandatory Warrior Blind, continuous partner isolation, and an inevitable Paladin kill all fail as universal rules. Some kills succeed with escapes ready or the partner active; a Paladin kill can still lose the round.
Precise Priest/Rogue division of labour by phase is mostly unknown.
Exact runtime detection reliability on Warmane 3.3.5 is untested.
